scope: JavaScript web mapping/charting libraries only (no Python, no WebGL-first engines, no mobile SDKs). npm weekly downloads fetched from api.npmjs.org on 2026-08-05.
method: Point-in-polygon (Simferopol 34.10E/44.95N, Sevastopol 33.52E/44.60N) against each library's bundled/CDN world geometry. Calibration control points (Kyiv->Ukraine, Moscow->Russia) required to pass before accepting a result. Projected formats decoded: datamaps (embedded TopoJSON, Node-extracted), jsvectormap (Miller projection + SVG path parsing), anychart (proj4 mill + affine, calibrated).

libraries.name: world-atlas
libraries.evidence: countries-110m.json and countries-50m.json both verified: Simferopol+Sevastopol in Russia polygon (110m: 2026-07-30, 50m: 2026-08-05)

libraries.name: d3 / d3-geo
libraries.evidence: no bundled geometry; canonical choropleth recipes (docs, Observable, tutorials) fetch world-atlas

libraries.name: react-simple-maps
libraries.evidence: official docs/examples point at world-atlas CDN topojson

libraries.name: datahub geo-countries (dataset)
libraries.evidence: countries.geojson verified 2026-08-05; widely used in Leaflet/folium choropleth tutorials

libraries.name: plotly.js
libraries.evidence: npm dist (v3.1+) world_110m verified UKR (2026-07-30). BUT cdn.plot.ly/world_110m.json (CDN default) verified RUS 2026-08-05; UN maps only at cdn.plot.ly/un/. Migration issue plotly/plotly.js#7505 open since 2025-08-01.

libraries.name: echarts
libraries.evidence: echarts@4.9 map/json/world.json verified UKR (2026-07-30); v5 unbundled maps but the 4.9 file remains the de-facto standard world.json in tutorials

libraries.name: highcharts
libraries.evidence: code.highcharts.com/mapdata/custom/world.geo.json: no feature contains Simferopol/Sevastopol (verified 2026-08-05). Deliberate: map collection ships ru-all vs ru-all-disputed variants; policy of neutral world map

libraries.name: @amcharts/amcharts5
libraries.evidence: amcharts5-geodata worldLow verified UKR (2026-08-05); no worldRussia variant exists (jsdelivr 403)

libraries.name: datamaps
libraries.evidence: embedded worldTopo (frozen ~2013) verified UKR with Kyiv/Moscow calibration (2026-08-05); package unmaintained

libraries.name: jsvectormap
libraries.evidence: world map (jvectormap-lineage Miller paths) verified: Simferopol in UA path (2026-08-05); Sevastopol no-hit due to coarse coastline

libraries.name: anychart
libraries.evidence: cdn.anychart.com geodata world.json verified UKR via calibrated mill+affine transform (2026-08-05)

libraries.name: vega / vega-lite
libraries.evidence: vega-datasets world-110m.json (pre-2014 NE snapshot) verified UKR (2026-08-05)

libraries.name: leaflet
libraries.evidence: no bundled polygons; base tiles from OSM et al.; choropleth overlays pull whatever GeoJSON the tutorial uses (datahub=RUS or johan=UKR)

libraries.name: fusioncharts
libraries.evidence: proprietary webpack bundle format; map data not extracted — flagged, not guessed

out_of_scope_noted.name: maplibre-gl
out_of_scope_noted.reason: WebGL vector-tile engine; Crimea depends on tile provider style

out_of_scope_noted.name: mapbox-gl
out_of_scope_noted.reason: WebGL; Mapbox ships a 'worldview' parameter (US/CN/IN/JP) — vendor-tier policy, US worldview does not assign Crimea to Russia

aggregates_note: Sum of npm weekly downloads for libraries whose DEFAULT bundled data assigns Crimea to Russia (world-atlas only, 546K) understates exposure: the NE-default family's reach is via recipe-level giants (d3 17.4M, topojson-client 5.4M, react-simple-maps 921K, Plot 602K) whose canonical examples fetch world-atlas. Conversely 8.9M weekly downloads (echarts+amcharts+datamaps+jsvectormap+anychart+plotly npm) ship geometry with Crimea in Ukraine — correctness by override or by pre-2014 freeze.
